raw_response:
I will keep my land in a simple pattern that fits my labor and water. Some people in my family work off-farm, so I do not want a plan that is too scattered or too hard to manage. I will put 10.1 mu into cotton because that is still my main money crop, but I will not push it too hard with excessive fertilizer because that raises cost and pest pressure. I will keep 8.0 mu in the wheat-maize rotation because it is steady, easier to manage with machinery, and gives me grain security and stable output. I will keep 4.0 mu in stevia because it can bring cash income, but I will limit the area since it needs more careful field management and marketing is less certain than grain.

I have well irrigation, so I will use water to protect yield at the key times rather than irrigate too often. I will use hybrid seed for maize and cotton to keep yield stable, improved seed for wheat, and improved planting material for stevia. On cotton I will use more potassium because I care about boll setting and plant strength. On wheat and maize I will keep fertilizer moderate and practical. I will not make the plan too complicated because after 35 years of farming, I know the safest money usually comes from doing the basic work on time: land preparation, sowing at the right window, enough fertilizer, timely irrigation, and pest control only as much as needed.
